https://www.worldfishing.net/news/fisher.text: FISHERIES Latvian fisheries association joins Europêche 1 year ago The Latvian North Atlantic Fisheries Association has become the latest member to join Europêche, strengthening the voice of the European sector at EU and international levels. Daniel Voces, managing director of Europêche said the organisation was delighted to welcome the latest signatory. “Their operational knowledge of the Baltic Sea, along with their active engagement in the Atlantic and international fishing areas, will bring valuable insight and perspective to our collective work,” he said. “This membership marks a new chapter in our mission to represent the interests of European fishers with a unified and stronger voice.” On behalf of the Latvian North Atlantic Fisheries Association, Jānis Leja, member of the management board, added: “We are honoured to join Europêche and become part of a strong and respected alliance of fisheries organisations. Our association is committed to promoting sustainable and science-based fisheries management. “We bring extensive experience from both regional and international fisheries, and we look forward to contributing actively to Europêche’s advocacy and policy development work.” Europêche said it looks forward to a productive partnership with the Latvian North Atlantic Fisheries Association and to working together toward a sustainable, competitive and resilient future for European fisheries. Turkish police raid Halk TV in Istanbul, sparking outrage over media freedom Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 14/10/2026 - 16:59 GMT+2 Police barricades surrounded the headquarters of Halk TV in Istanbul on Wednesday, 14 October, as Turkish authorities raided the independent broadcaster and appointed a trustee to take control of its operations. … More Financial crime investigators searched the building, forcing a temporary suspension of broadcasts. Prosecutors accused the channel's chairman, Cafer Mahiroglu , of bid rigging, bribery and money laundering. Of the 17 people sought by investigators, 11 were detained. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Mahiroglu, who lives abroad, rejected the allegations, calling the takeover politically motivated. Outside the building, supporters gathered to defend the channel's journalists, while opposition politicians and press freedom organisations condemned the intervention. The case has raised fresh concerns about media freedom in Turkey, where independent news outlets face longstanding political pressure. Halk TV is known for its critical coverage of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's government. It has also reported extensively on the legal troubles of Ekrem Imamoglu , Istanbul's jailed mayor and one of Erdogan's main political rivals. Opposition MP Ali Mahir Basarir warned against taking control of media organisations simply because they criticise the government. Amnesty International called for the broadcaster's independence to be restored. Turkey stands 163rd out of 180 countries in Reporters Without Borders' press freedom ranking.
